name: apple-calendar-mcp
description: Read and manage macOS Calendar events through EventKit, without ever editing the past
long_description:
A local MCP server written in Swift that gives Claude access to the Calendar app on this Mac.

There is no network, no account and no API key. iCloud is only the sync engine that fills the local calendar store. The gate is macOS privacy consent, and the grant appears under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Calendars. Full access is required: write-only access cannot read events back, so the server could neither confirm what it created nor enforce the rule below.

Finished events are never modified or deleted. A past event is the record of what happened, and this server refuses to rewrite it even when asked — though an event still in progress can be edited, so an overrunning meeting can be extended.

Plug and play: there is nothing to configure. Every calendar is reachable; the only control over this server is its own per-tool permission switch below.

EventKit cannot invite attendees and cannot create repeating events; both must be done in Calendar.app.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple Inc.

tools.name: calendar_status
tools.description: Report whether Calendar access is granted, and how to grant it. Reads no events.

tools.name: calendars_list
tools.description: List calendars, their accounts, and which accept writes

tools.name: calendar_search
tools.description: Find events in a date range, optionally filtered by text and calendar

tools.name: calendar_get
tools.description: Read one event in full, including whether it can still be edited

tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Add an event. Cannot invite attendees or create a repeating series.

tools.name: update_event
tools.description: Change an event. Refuses events that have already ended.

tools.name: delete_event
tools.description: Permanently delete an event. Requires explicit confirmation; refuses events that have ended.
